# CLI buildout rules (plugin) — run ONCE during repo creation, then discarded.
# One-time structural checks on the project split and the release-asset naming
# contract; the ongoing CLI judgment (output/exit-code contract, new commands and
# clients joining the graph) lives in shapes/cli.llmlint.yml.
version: 1.1

rules:
  - name: asset_naming_contract_shared
    description: |
      true when every install surface that downloads a release asset (an install
      script, a Homebrew/Scoop manifest, a CI job) constructs the SAME archive and
      `.sha256` name the release workflow produced, from one shared naming scheme.
      false when a surface hardcodes an asset name that can drift from what the
      release job uploads.
    files:
      include:
        - ".github/workflows/**"
        - "**/install*.sh"
        - "**/*.rb"
        - "**/*.json"
        - "**/*formula*"
    relevance: the repo distributes downloadable release assets across more than one install surface

  - name: cli_split_from_its_e2e_and_externals
    description: |
      true when the command and its fast unit tests are one project, the suite that
      installs and drives the built command is a separate project depending on it,
      and each external system the command talks to is its own project carrying its
      own live-service suite. false when the subprocess-level suite sits inside the
      CLI project — so every change spawns the binary — or when a client for an
      external system has no project of its own, so a change to argument parsing
      reaches the network.
    files:
      include: ["nx.json", "**/project.json", "**/e2e/**", "**/tests/**"]
